page: Microsoft Azure E2ds_v7 is a memory-optimized virtual machine instance powered by a dedicated Intel Xeon 6973P-C processor. Operating on the x86_64 architecture under the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor, this instance features 2 vCPUs mapped to 1 physical core with hyper-threading enabled. It is equipped with 16.0 GB of system memory, yielding a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8.0 GB per core. The hardware configuration also includes a 118 GB local SSD and supports Premium Storage.

Benchmark data reveals moderate single-core capabilities alongside constrained multi-core performance. The single-core stress-ng CPU test scores 2215.58, placing it in the average tier, whereas the multi-core stress-ng score of 2263.98 is categorized as poor. Memory performance is mixed; the Passmark memory score is average at 1927.71, but large-block uncached read and write bandwidths are poor at 22.92 GB/sec and 12.15 GB/sec respectively. For database operations, the instance achieves a weak Passmark database score of 1429.99 and processes 4.01 million Redis SET operations per second.

From a resource density perspective, the E2ds_v7 offers qualitative cost efficiency for workloads that demand high memory capacity relative to compute power without requiring extensive multi-core processing. The inclusion of advanced CPU instruction sets, such as AVX-512 and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX), assists in accelerating specific vector and matrix operations, as evidenced by an average small-model LLM text generation speed of 88.94 tokens per second. This instance is best suited for small-scale databases, caching layers, light web serving, and memory-bound applications that do not scale heavily across multiple threads.
description: Microsoft Azure E2ds_v7 is a memory-optimized virtual machine featuring 2 vCPUs and 16.0 GB of RAM, powered by a dedicated Intel Xeon 6973P-C processor running at 4.2 GHz. Built on the x86_64 architecture with Microsoft Hyper-V, it includes a 118 GB local SSD and supports Premium Storage. Benchmarks indicate average single-core CPU performance with a stress-ng score of 2215.58, though multi-core and large-block memory bandwidth benchmarks fall into lower percentiles. The instance features advanced instruction sets like Intel AMX and AVX-512, which support specialized vector operations. Qualitatively, this configuration provides a cost-efficient profile for memory-intensive workloads that do not require high multi-threaded compute scaling. It is suitable for small-scale databases, caching layers, and memory-bound enterprise applications.
